title: Tuning from intrinsic to disorder-dominated quantum states in a kagome antiferromagnet
authors: Y. Tanaka, R. Kumakura, T. Yamaguchi, M. Kato, K. Totsuka, B. Li, Y. Zhao, Y. Li, R. Grasset, O. Cavani, A. Alessi, V. Sharma, Y. Kohama, S. Suetsugu
abstract: The spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet (AFM) provides a paradigmatic platform for realizing quantum spin-liquid (QSL) and magnetization-plateau states. Experimental progress, however, has been hindered by structural disorder, whose effects on these quantum states remain elusive. A key experimental challenge is therefore to connect intrinsic and disorder-dominated regimes through controlled disorder and identify emergent degrees of freedom associated with disorder. Here we introduce controlled point defects through electron irradiation into the spin-1/2 kagome AFM YCu3(OH)6.5Br2.5 (YCOB) and track the resulting evolution of its low-energy magnetic states. High-field magnetic torque measurements reveal that the 1/9 and 1/3 magnetization plateaus are strongly suppressed by only ~0.05% irradiation-induced defects, demonstrating that these delicate quantum many-body states are extraordinarily fragile against dilute disorder. Moreover, the irradiation induces a sign reversal of the magnetic torque only at low temperatures and low fields, indicating the emergence of correlated defect-induced moments rather than isolated free spins. Remarkably, the characteristic scaling of the magnetic specific heat, absent in pristine YCOB, progressively emerges with increasing disorder. These findings establish dilute disorder as an effective tuning parameter that drives the kagome AFM from intrinsic quantum states toward a disorder-dominated regime. The contrasting responses further identify pristine YCOB as an exceptionally clean kagome AFM for accessing intrinsic quantum states.
summary: This work investigates the quantum magnetic behavior of a kagome antiferromagnet by systematically introducing controlled disorder via electron irradiation. By measuring magnetic torque and specific heat, the researchers show that the system's intrinsic quantum states are highly fragile to disorder, which acts as a tunable parameter driving the system into a disorder-dominated regime. This establishes the material as a key platform for studying disorder effects in quantum magnets.
main_problem: The study aims to understand how the quantum magnetic states of a kagome antiferromagnet evolve when tuned from their intrinsic quantum regime toward a disorder-dominated regime.
main_result: The research demonstrates that the delicate magnetization plateaus are extremely fragile against minute amounts of disorder, and the emergence of disorder leads to characteristic scaling behaviors in the magnetic specific heat.
method: The authors used controlled point defects, introduced via electron irradiation, on single crystals of the kagome antiferromagnet YCu3(OH)6.5Br2.5 (YCOB).
model_or_system: The system is a spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet (AFM). The experimental platform involves measuring magnetic torque, specific heat, and magnetization on pristine versus irradiated samples.
key_observables: Magnetization plateaus (1/9 and 1/3), magnetic torque sign reversal, and the characteristic scaling of the magnetic specific heat ($C/T$ vs $T/H$).
important_parameters: Controlled disorder level, quantified by electron irradiation fluence ($\phi$), which acts as the tuning parameter.
main_assumptions: The defect density calculated from electron scattering cross sections represents an upper limit, as annealing during measurement could reduce the actual defect concentration.
figures_summary: Figures show the suppression of magnetization plateaus and magnetic torque anomalies with increasing disorder, and the progressive emergence of characteristic scaling behavior in the specific heat as disorder increases.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares measurements (torque, specific heat, susceptibility) on pristine versus irradiated samples, using the degree of disorder as the primary tuning parameter to map the transition between intrinsic and disorder-dominated quantum states.
why_interesting: The study provides a clean, tunable experimental realization of disorder effects on quantum ground states, which is highly relevant for understanding quantum phase transitions in strongly correlated materials.
